claims: NASA is targeting Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. ET for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission launch is from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B.
The launch window for the Artemis II mission is two hours long and extends until 8:24 p.m. ET.
There is an 80% chance of favorable weather for the Artemis II launch.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
The launch window for the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026 is 6:24 p.m. to 8:24 p.m. ET.
The official NASA broadcast for the Artemis II launch begins at 12:50 p.m. ET.
Cryogenic propellant loading for the Artemis II mission starts around 7:45 a.m. ET.
The Artemis II astronauts head to the pad approximately 4 hours and 40 minutes before liftoff.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day test flight.
The Artemis II mission will test and evaluate the Orion spacecraft's life support systems.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew will travel around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew will not land on the Moon.
If delayed, the Artemis II launch window remains open through April 6.
There is another launch opportunity for the Artemis II mission around April 30.
